clue.text: Lusty pics nonce cut out

indicators.note: out in the sense of wrong or disordered, telling us to rearrange the three words before it

explanation.surface: A prudish editor slices racy pictures, judging them too lustful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals an anagram of PICS NONCE CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Concupiscent means full of sexual desire, an elevated synonym for lusty.

clue.text: Endlessly humble wiseacre

indicators.note: without its ends, so the synonym for humble loses both its first and last letters

parts.note: lowly means humble

explanation.surface: A know-all who never stops being modest would be a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' strips the L and Y from LOWLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is someone who acts wise, and the owl is the proverbial image of wisdom, used of a solemn would-be sage.

clue.text: Switched mail order with inferior packaging that's made of recycled waste

indicators.note: packaging means wrapping round, so the word for inferior encloses the other pieces

parts.note: cheap means inferior, shoddy

indicators.note: switched means swapped, so the two pieces for mail and order appear in the opposite order to the clue

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
post means mail

explanation.surface: A firm switches its mail-order business to cheap packaging made from recycled waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mail order' reads as one phrase but splits in two, and 'Switched' swaps them to give OMPOST; 'packaging' wraps the inferior word round that.
explanation.definitionFit: A compost heap is a pile of garden and kitchen refuse left to rot down into reusable soil, so it is made of recycled waste.

clue.text: Exercises help us to get money

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
SOS is the distress call, a plea of help us

explanation.surface: A fitness instructor's workouts might help clients get money.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesos are the currency units of Mexico and several other Latin American countries, so they are money.

clue.text: Throw up after meat, so outwardly chaotic

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so the word for so wraps round the rest

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus, used in quoted text

indicators.note: after puts the throw piece behind the meat in the answer

parts.note: ham is a meat

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for throw is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lob means throw

explanation.surface: Someone vomiting after a meaty meal looks a mess from the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' looks like vomiting, but in a down clue 'up' reverses the throw word; 'after' orders the pieces and 'outwardly' has the Latin for 'so' wrap round HAMBOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambolic is informal British for disorganised and messy, a synonym for chaotic.

clue.text: Twiddle one's thumbs when ending letter

indicators.note: ending here asks for the final letter of each of the three words that describe the idle pastime

explanation.surface: Someone bored waits for something to end, twiddling their thumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ess is the spelt-out name of the alphabet character S, so it is a letter.

clue.text: A number failed to stop the try when playing English

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the word for failed sits inside the other letters
playing means being moved about, so the letters of the try are rearranged

parts.note: went means failed, as in a bulb that went

explanation.surface: In a rugby match, a failure to stop the English try came while playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when playing' makes TYTHRE from THE TRY; with E that is TYTHREE, and 'to stop' puts WENT inside after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-three is an integer, so it is a number.

clue.text: Number-one cognitive quality

parts.note: looking after number one means looking after yourself, so a mental quality concerning number one is consciousness of oneself

explanation.walkthrough: 'Number-one' looks like a ranking, the top cognitive quality, but it is slang for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is conscious knowledge of one's own character and feelings, a mental faculty centred on the self.

clue.text: Gossips in unruly rabble spout nonsense for circulating

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the two letters for nonsense surround everything else

parts.note: BS is a vulgar abbreviation for nonsense

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, telling us to rearrange the letters of rabble

parts.note: to mouth is to spout words, speak pompously

explanation.surface: Rumour-mongers in a disorderly crowd talk rubbish to spread it about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges the crowd word to LABBER, and 'for circulating' has the nonsense letters wrap round the whole, splitting so B starts and S ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Blabbermouths are people who cannot keep secrets and talk indiscreetly, the same as gossips.

clue.text: Grasps one dumped in ditch in terrible condition?

indicators.note: dumped in means thrown into, so the pieces go inside the word for ditch

parts.note: ea is a dialect word for a river or a drainage channel in the Fens
clamps means grasps tightly
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone seizes another and throws them into a ditch, leaving them in a terrible state.
explanation.walkthrough: EA is an old word for a Fenland drainage channel. The question mark signals that the definition is a loose description.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclampsia is a dangerous pregnancy disorder involving seizures, a grave medical condition.

clue.text: Turn page, interrupting trick

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the letter for page goes inside the word for trick

parts.note: a sell is a hoax or trick

explanation.surface: Someone turns a page in the middle of performing a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a period or stint, as is a turn, as in 'take a turn at the wheel'.

clue.text: Fellow rep offering blood products

parts.note: rep is short for repertory, a theatre company of actors

explanation.surface: A colleague who is a sales representative is offering blood products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rep' looks like a sales representative, but it is a repertory company.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotting factors such as factor VIII are proteins extracted from donated plasma and sold as blood products.

clue.text: Groomed families welcoming European asylum

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the word for families encloses the European letter

parts.note: clans are families
a haven is a refuge or asylum

explanation.surface: Smartened-up families welcome a European seeking asylum.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean-shaven describes a man with no beard or stubble, one way of being well groomed.

clue.text: City bar rejected personal-hygiene equipment

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for bar is read backwards

parts.note: but means bar, as in 'all but him' meaning except him

explanation.surface: A city pub is rejected for having no washing facilities.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is a city in south-west England famous for Roman baths. 'rejected' turns BUT into TUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathtub is the vessel you wash your body in, equipment for personal hygiene.

clue.text: Toxic pro hit out, loosening up when shaken?

indicators.note: out in the sense of wrong or disordered, so the letters of the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poisonous professional lashes out, loosening up once shaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals an anagram of TOXIC PRO HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Thixotropic gels, like non-drip paint, become runnier when stirred or shaken, so they loosen up under agitation.

clue.text: Appetiser containing a mostly whitish flour

indicators.note: containing means holding, so the word for appetiser goes round the letter a

parts.note: a whet is something that sharpens the appetite

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the synonym for whitish loses its final letter

parts.note: mealy means pale, whitish

explanation.surface: A starter contains a mostly pale flour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appetiser' looks like a starter course, but it is the old sense of something that sharpens the appetite. 'containing' and 'mostly' do the building.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheatmeal is brown flour milled from wheat with some of the bran retained.

clue.text: Synthetic tongue person ate anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means haphazardly, so the letters of person ate are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone ate an artificial tongue in a careless manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' signals an anagram of PERSON ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an artificial language devised by Zamenhof in 1887, a constructed tongue.

clue.text: First to join ends of optical nerve fibre

parts.note: 1ST is first, with the digit read as the letter I

indicators.note: ends of picks out the final letter of optical and the final letter of nerve

explanation.surface: The first step is to join the ends of an optic nerve fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' is written 1ST, with the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a tough plant fibre from Mexican agave and yucca, used for cord and brushes.

clue.text: Align compass and sail along

definitions.meaning: to set in a row, to line up
to ... a coast is to sail along it

explanation.surface: A navigator lines up a compass and sails along the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Range covers arranging in rows, the extent or compass of something, and coasting along a shore.

clue.text: Prima ballerina assoluta about to follow movie symbol for text?

indicators.note: to follow puts the dancer piece after the movie piece in the answer

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a movie

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the dancer's name is read backwards

parts.note: Margot Fonteyn was named prima ballerina assoluta of the Royal Ballet

explanation.surface: A great ballerina is about to appear after a film, a symbol in a text message?
explanation.walkthrough: Margot Fonteyn held the rare title prima ballerina assoluta. 'about' turns MARGOT into TOGRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A pictogram is a picture standing for a word or idea, the kind of icon used in place of writing.

clue.text: Incompetent fusion of Japanese and short musical dramas

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese musical drama

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: opera is musical drama

explanation.surface: A clumsy production blends Japanese theatre with brief operas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts OPERA to OPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone with no chance of success, an incompetent person.

clue.text: Vulgarian charge overturned prior to brief rendezvous

indicators.note: prior to puts the charge piece before the meeting-place piece
overturned means upended, so the word for charge is read backwards

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the meeting-place word loses its last letter

parts.note: a venue is a rendezvous, a meeting place

explanation.surface: A vulgar person's charge is quashed just before a short date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns RAP into PAR; 'brief' cuts VENUE to VENU.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is an upstart with new money but no refinement, so a vulgarian.

clue.text: Spring frost after 2nd of April

indicators.note: after here puts the frost piece behind the month's letter
2nd of picks out the second letter of the month's name

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: Spring frost arrives in early April.
explanation.definitionFit: The prime of something is its springtime, its early, flourishing stage.

clue.text: Cardinal quits after getting back to front

indicators.note: back to front means its rear letter is taken to the front

parts.note: evens means quits, all square

explanation.surface: A cardinal resigns after returning to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman, but it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is a cardinal number, one used for counting.

clue.text: And not the last sightings of Captain Horatio Hornblower

indicators.note: the last sightings means the last letters seen of each word of the naval hero's name

explanation.surface: These were not the final glimpses of the fictional naval captain.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatio Hornblower is C.S. Forester's Napoleonic-era naval hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Nor joins a further negative, meaning and not.

clue.text: Man turning something that won't come free without power tool

indicators.note: turning means turning round, so the man's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ian is a man's name

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the meal goes round the letter for power

parts.note: there's no such thing as a free lunch, says the proverb
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A man fails to free something stuck without using a power tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power tool' looks like the definition, but 'power' is P and 'tool' alone defines. 'without' means outside, and 'turning' gives NAI.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail punch is a hand tool for driving nail heads below a wood surface.

clue.text: Shag and doze off

definitions.meaning: shag means the pile on a carpet or cloth, as in shagpile
doze off means drop off briefly to sleep

explanation.surface: A cheeky pair of activities to end on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shag' looks like British slang for sex, but here it is the raised pile of a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nap is the raised fibres on cloth and also a short sleep.

clue.text: Slender leak causing squeak

parts.note: narrow means slender
an escape of gas or water is a leak

explanation.surface: A thin leak in a pipe makes a squeaking noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeak' looks like a sound, but it is the British informal 'a narrow squeak', a close shave.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow squeak, or just a squeak, is a close call: an escape that only just succeeded.
